With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment continue to strengthen; maintaining the policy rate near zero and ongoing Treasury and agency MBS purchases is consistent with Taylor‑rule and New Keynesian guidance (e.g., Clarida–Galí–Gertler) to stay accommodative while the output gap closes and inflation—largely viewed as transitory—does not de‑anchor expectations. This approach leverages balance‑sheet tools to ease credit and financial frictions (Bernanke; Monacelli) and uses an average‑inflation‑targeting framework to keep expectations anchored around 2 percent (Svensson), supporting recovery while acknowledging virus‑related risks.
